items.title: George "Happy" Schilling Interview, 1957-09-08
items.q: And then, when George was playing center saxophone, this was supposed to be a brass band, man, they were heavy. And they had, uh, Eddie Iman from Pace, a suit of phone, he bought that suit of phone from Mackey. Lefty Iman. He bought that suit of phone from Mackey.

ctx.x: Yeah, on a New Year's Eve night, playing for this big lumberman up in Kansas, the only girl for pleasure, yeah, I'll go play. They had to hire six men for New Year's Eve, that was the union's law. I wouldn't have got in on that job, because he hadn't made a contract before, the union said they had to have six. So they got me on bass and another fellow on guitar, some Italian fellow. They went there and the job paid thirty dollars. Each hour overtime was ten dollars an hour, we would pay three hours overtime. That…
This show you were talking about, they advertised it as a jazz band, do you say?
